page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-16 is an x86_64 architecture instance within the e2 server family. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores from an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1.0 GB per core allocation. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmarks show a mix of strong single-core performance alongside average multi-core and memory capabilities. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance is rated as strong, whereas multi-core performance falls into the average category. Memory bandwidth tests yield average results, with read-only cached small block speeds at 645.66 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 35.27 GB/sec. However, single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, perform poorly, placing in the bottom 10% of benchmarks.

Given its high vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance is structured for compute-heavy tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. It achieves average performance in software compilation, ray tracing, and static web serving. This profile makes it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads like CI/CD pipelines, web serving, and lightweight multi-threaded processing where CPU allocation is prioritized over memory capacity.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-16 is an x86_64 compute-focused instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz with a 16 MB L3 cache. Lacking local storage and GPU accelerators, it allocates 1.0 GB of memory per core. Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, while multi-core execution, memory bandwidth, and database operations perform at average levels. Conversely, single-threaded compression and decompression tasks show weak performance. This instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-heavy workloads with moderate memory requirements, such as software compilation, static web serving, and multi-threaded processing pipelines.
